issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: the problem statement (text and UML) specifies a two-parameter signature addGuestStudents(int, String) — an int number of new guest students and a String reason — but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This discrepancy (1) appears in the problem statement text (problem_statement.md line 50) and the UML (problem_statement.md line 73) and (2) is implemented in the solution at solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java (signature at line 90). The mismatch will confuse students about which signature to implement and can cause automated tests or examples that expect the two-parameter signature to fail or be incompatible with the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution method signature to include the reason parameter: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) (and handle, store, or explicitly ignore/log the reason) and update the solution code accordingly (file: solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, signature at line 90), or (B) if the reason parameter is not needed, update the problem statement text and UML to declare addGuestStudents(int) and adjust the task description (problem_statement.md lines ~50 and ~73) and the template comments so all three artifacts match. Also ensure the template's TODO and any tests reflect the chosen signature.
